content: Early blight (Alternaria solani) on tomato presents as dark brown circular lesions with concentric rings. Apply copper-based fungicide or chlorothalonil every 7-10 days. Remove infected lower leaves. Ensure adequate plant spacing for air circulation.

Late blight (Phytophthora infestans) spreads rapidly in cool, wet conditions. Water-soaked grey lesions on leaves. Apply metalaxyl or mancozeb fungicide immediately. Destroy infected plants. Do not compost.

Gray leaf spot (Cercospora zeae-maydis) presents as rectangular gray to tan lesions parallel to leaf veins. Use foliar fungicide (azoxystrobin or pyraclostrobin) at early tasseling. Select resistant varieties in future plantings.

Powdery mildew (Blumeria graminis) appears as white powdery patches on leaf surfaces. Apply triadimefon or propiconazole fungicide at early infection stage. Improve air circulation and avoid excess nitrogen fertilization.

Rice blast (Magnaporthe oryzae) causes diamond-shaped lesions with gray centers and brown borders. Apply tricyclazole or azoxystrobin fungicide preventively. Maintain proper water management. Use resistant varieties.

Water stress symptoms include wilting, leaf curl, and yellowing. Measure soil moisture at root zone. Irrigate deeply and infrequently to encourage deep root development. Avoid overhead irrigation; use drip irrigation where possible.
